maintenance.verified_defect: Connection/setup, lock or page-budget failures all shrank the history page, with no recovery from a one-row cap.
maintenance.additional_verified_health_defect: Different consumers/lanes could inherit one aggregate warning timer despite committed progress between failures, falsely presenting rotating intermittent failures as one sustained outage.

close_race.root_cause: Synchronous reduce-only refusal was classified as UNKNOWN; query recovery recognized a different rejection code but not this one, leaving a known refusal nonterminal forever.

context_expiry.reproduced_defect: Expired market or signal context was converted into generic ValueError/UNAVAILABLE, stopping the peer batch instead of terminating or retrying only the affected candidate.

changes.close_rejection: Exact CLOSE/reduce-only HTTP400/-2022 is REJECTED. Old UNKNOWN additionally needs matching durable original refusal and explicit current order absence. Found/bound/filled orders retain their normal reconciliation path. Lock-time evidence checks and exact terminal idempotency protect concurrent recovery.
changes.context: Validated expiry maps to existing candidate-level waits; malformed/future/scope/evidence failures still fail closed. Signal deadline is rechecked after account reads.
changes.history: Fixed-stage safe diagnostics distinguish setup, locks and commit from page processing. Eight full committed low-cost pages plus cooldown permit conservative 25-percent capacity probes; failed probes revert to the last stable cap.
changes.maintenance_health: Persist separate consumer/lane failure intervals. Only same-lane newer committed evidence after fault onset or explicit strictly newer recovery breaks continuity. Unknown, hot expiry and worker faults remain independent. Missing/stale/same/future timestamps never prove recovery. Current failures remain visible; the original 120-second alert threshold is unchanged.

release.background_history_retry_evidence: After restart, setup consumed 150-205ms of a 250ms page budget on two observed failed pages. These were classified SETUP_PRESSURE_OR_UNKNOWN and did not shrink the page. Later pages committed and advanced; caps remained 250-1000, not one row. Underlying setup jitter remains unproven.
release.background_auto_growth_evidence_at_11434: Committed s6:s3 discovery cap 243 with 5 recoveries; cold expiry cap 390 with 2 recoveries; s8:s3 discovery cap 243 with 5 recoveries; TV discovery cap 487 with 3 recoveries. Intermittent failed pages were still exposed in diagnostics.

health_lane_hotfix.acceptance_defect: Health's initial timestamp preceded a slow database query. A genuinely completed cycle read during that query could finish after the initial timestamp, so the new future-time check incorrectly discarded valid maintenance recovery evidence. Main trading continued, but alarm acceptance was not declared passed.

health_clock_final.clock_contract: Only maintenance evidence validation and maintenance elapsed time use a real post-read local clock; stored as maintenance_observed_at_ms. Original queue-lag clocks remain unchanged. Source timestamps never set or expand the local clock, and genuinely future evidence is still rejected.

review_fixes: Import-verifier output contract corrected before deployment; covered by an executing verifier-contract unit test.
Identical concurrent rejection recovery now verifies the committed terminal proof and returns idempotently instead of reporting a false conflict.

boundaries: No guarantee that every future venue/network/database exception disappears.
Unknown submission outcomes without original conclusive refusal still require reconciliation and explicit alerts, never blind resubmission.
Maintenance timeout category is a bounded-control diagnostic, not proof of database capacity shortage.
No claim of improved profitability or LIVE acceptance.
